summary: Bergland tower in Ottawa National Forest; a 1953 windstorm destroyed an older 100-foot steel tower on the site, and a replacement was announced. NHLR-registered 2021.

events.note: A windstorm blew down a 100-foot steel fire watch tower near Bergland; the report calls it more than 20 years old and completely destroyed
Announced July 7, 1953 that a new tower would be set up at the site, to be moved from a secondary watch point. The sources read do not report completion
Registered January 8, 2021 as US 1416, MI 6; nominated by John Strasser

evidence.supports: believed built in the 1950s, around the time White Pine was established
evidence.quote: This tower is believed to have been built in the 1950s, around the time the town of White Pine and its company homes were established

evidence.supports: administered by the U.S. Forest Service
a windstorm near Bergland blew down a tower
evidence.quote: one blown down near Bergland during a windstorm last week

evidence.supports: the blown-down steel tower was more than 20 years old and completely destroyed
evidence.quote: The 100-foot steel tower which was blown down was more than 20 years old and was completely destroyed

evidence.supports: state conservation department officials announced a replacement at the same site
evidence.quote: State conservation department officials announced today that a new forest fire watch tower will be set up at the site of one blown down near Bergland during a windstorm last week

evidence.supports: a replacement would be moved from a secondary watch point to the Bergland site
evidence.quote: The new tower already is being used at a secondary watch point and will be transported to the Bergland site

evidence.supports: no one hurt; the watchman was off duty
evidence.quote: No one was injured since the watchman had gone off duty for the night when the storm hit

sources.title: Bergland (Forest Lookouts page quoting a Record-Eagle report of July 7, 1953)

corrections.proposed: remove unless a source for the current tower is found
corrections.why: The only 100-foot figure in the sources describes the steel tower blown down in 1953, not the tower standing today; no source read gives the current tower's height

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register believes the tower dates from the 1950s. The 1953 report describes an older tower destroyed on this site and a replacement planned for it. The sources read do not show which tower stands today, so no build year is recorded beyond the 1953 events.

notes_for_editor: Status 'standing' from the brief is not supported by any source read, so it is omitted from facts; the firelookout.org Michigan page returned no Bergland entry. Access and staffing unknown. The brief's 30.5 m height likely comes from the 100-foot figure in the 1953 report, which describes the destroyed tower. Only two sources; a further search for the Michigan tower list or a recent status report could resolve status and the current tower's history.
